status_scale.discussion: talked about on a list or forum, no concrete proposal
status_scale.proposal: written proposal (BIP draft, design doc, PR description) not yet merged
status_scale.merged: merged into a project's main branch, not yet released
status_scale.released: shipped in a tagged release of that software
status_scale.documentation: specification or documentation change only; no software behavior changes

items.title: Peers are no longer disconnected for a missed ping while they are sending us blocks
items.what_happened: Bitcoin Core stops enforcing the 20-minute ping timeout against a peer while blocks are being downloaded from that peer.
items.why_it_matters: During initial block download on a slow link, a peer busy serving our block requests could miss the ping deadline and be dropped although it was not at fault. This avoids needless disconnects for low-bandwidth nodes.
items.not_yet: In master only; not in a release. No consensus or policy change.

items.title: Private transaction broadcast now always completes all three initial connections
items.what_happened: When a node initiates a private broadcast of a transaction, it now completes all three initial broadcast connections instead of stopping early when the transaction comes back or conflicts.
items.why_it_matters: Stopping early could leak timing information that helps link a transaction to its origin. The PR addresses theoretical timing attacks raised in earlier review of the private-broadcast work.
affects: users who broadcast transactions privately through Bitcoin Core
items.not_yet: In master only; not in a release. Check release notes for when private broadcast and this fix ship.
items.uncertainty: The attacks addressed are described as theoretical in the PR.

items.title: Wallets record which client version last opened and decrypted them
items.what_happened: The wallet now records the version of the last Bitcoin Core client that opened it and that decrypted it.
items.why_it_matters: Groundwork for future automatic wallet upgrades: if a wallet is upgraded, opened in an older version, then opened in a newer one again, the newer client can detect this and redo the upgrade instead of leaving mixed upgraded and non-upgraded data.
affects: wallet users who switch between Bitcoin Core versions
items.not_yet: In master only; no new automatic upgrade ships with this change. It prepares for later ones.

items.title: PSBT type registry adds the missing PSBT_IN_P2C_TWEAK (0x19) entry
items.what_happened: The BIP-174 PSBT field registry now lists input key type 0x19, PSBT_IN_P2C_TWEAK, defined in BIP-372 (pay-to-contract tweak fields). It had been left out when the tables moved into the registry.
items.why_it_matters: The registry exists so new BIPs do not reuse a key type that is already taken. A missing row risks a collision in a future proposal.
items.not_yet: Documentation fix only; no change to consensus, node software or existing PSBT behavior.
